newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota recalls more than 260,000 cars.
newsitem.headline: Toyota recalls more than 260,000 cars.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Tuesday it told Japan's Transport Ministry it was recalling 260,000 diesel-engine cars in Japan and another 8,600 vehicles marketed overseas to repair engine and fuel injection components.
A faulty rubber plug in an engine cylinder and a component in the electronic fuel injection system could cause engines to overheat and stall, the company said.

The defective cars were made from June 1, 1994 through February 24, 1997. The recall affects 17 models, including Estima and Granvia minivans and HiLux and Land Cruiser sport-utility vehicles in Japan. Only two overseas models, the Land Cruiser and HiLux (4-Runner), were affected.
The 8,600 vehicles sold abroad included 5,800 vehicles sold in Europe and 2,000 in Latin America, a Toyota spokesman said.
The company will repair the defective cars free of charge, in accordance with each country's rules.
The total cost of the repairs is estimated at four billion yen in Japan and 200 million yen abroad, the spokesman said.
No accidents related to the defects had been reported in Japan, he said.
